title: Classic Lime Curd
story: Lime curd sounds like a project until you make it, and then it sounds like something you should have been making all along. Ten minutes of stirring, a quick strain, and you have two cups of something that makes everything it touches better. The yield sounds generous until it isn't.

items.text: ½ cup (120ml) fresh lime juice (about 4–5 limes)
½ cup (113g) unsalted butter, cut into small cubes

steps.text: In a medium heavy-bottomed saucepan, whisk together 6 egg yolks, 1 cup granulated sugar, ½ cup fresh lime juice, 2 tbsp lime zest, and ¼ tsp fine sea salt until smooth.
Place over medium-low heat. Cook, stirring constantly with a silicone spatula and making sure to scrape the bottom and corners of the pan.
steps.donenessCue: The curd is ready when it thickly coats the back of a spoon and holds a line when you drag a finger through it, about 8–12 minutes. Do not let it boil.

steps.text: Remove from heat. Immediately whisk in ½ cup cubed butter a few pieces at a time until completely smooth. Whisk in 1 tsp vanilla bean paste now if using.
Pour through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl or jar. This removes the zest and any bits of cooked egg and is what gives the curd its silky texture. Don't skip it.
Press plastic wrap directly against the surface of the curd to prevent a skin from forming. Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate. The curd will continue to thicken as it chills.

ifYouFeelLikeIt: Whisk in 1 tsp vanilla bean paste after removing from the heat for a softer, more dessert-like flavor.
Swap the limes for Meyer lemons for a floral, less assertive version. Good on angel food cake.
Stir into Greek yogurt for a quick lime fool — about 2 tablespoons per cup of yogurt, more if you want.
storage: Keeps refrigerated for up to 2 weeks with plastic wrap pressed against the surface. Does not freeze well.
